label: ex:bach-single-electron-buildup
title: Single-Electron Buildup (Bach et al. 2013)
html:
With the mask centered on the double-slit (P_{12} configuration), the electron source intensity was reduced to a detection rate of approximately 1 Hz. At 600 eV kinetic energy, the average distance between consecutive electrons was 2.3 \times 10^6 m, ensuring that only one electron was present in the 1 m system at any time and eliminating electron--electron interactions.

The electrostatic quadrupole lens was set to magnify the central five diffraction orders. Figure 3 of [bach2013] shows the buildup sequence:

Stage Electrons Observation
(a) 2 Random hits, no pattern
(b) 7 Random hits
(c) 209 Faint clustering visible
(d) 1004 Pattern discernible
(e) 6235 Clear five-order diffraction pattern

The final buildup took approximately 2 hours. The progression from apparently random individual detections to a coherent interference pattern demonstrates Feynman's point: each electron "interferes with itself" --- the wave function passes through both slits simultaneously, even though each electron is detected as a single localized event.
